label: Grounded Seitō feminist awakening in Zen meditative direct experience
description: Raichō Hiratsuka practiced intensive Rinzai-Sōtō Zen kenshō prior to founding Seitō (1911), framing women's creative self-awakening as dissolving dualistic subject-object alienation.
dialecticalTension: Transforms Zen non-dual inwardness into modern feminist cultural assertion.
historicalContext: Seitō inaugural manifesto ("In the Beginning, Woman Was the Sun", 1911).

citations.author: Raichō Hiratsuka
citations.work: In the Beginning, Woman Was the Sun (Autobiography)

label: Synthesized Nietzschean self-overcoming with Japanese feminist subjectivity
description: Hiratsuka drew enthusiastically on Nietzsche's Thus Spoke Zarathustra alongside Ellen Key to challenge conventional Japanese feminine modesty and proclaim autonomous self-creation.
dialecticalTension: Appropriates individualist self-overcoming for collective women's liberation.

citations.author: Jan Bardsley
